record.english: The above expansion on this point is indeed a valid one, given the following statement in the commentary to A Compendium of Higher Knowledge composed by Gyaltsab Je, Darma Rinchen: The Thirty Verses includes that statement that “they belong to the one where they've been born.”  As such, if a person is a being in the desire realm, then even if they achieve the fourth concentration level their negative consciousness is included into the level of desire.  As such, one must master the understanding of how a person at the preliminary stage of the first concentration level manifests negative emotions of the desire realm.

record.acip: DE LTAR YANG BZHI BRGYA PA LAS, ,DE NYID SHES PAS GAL TE 'DIR, ,MYA NGAN 'DAS PA MA THOB KYANG, ,SKYE BA GZHAN DU 'BAD MED PAR, ,NGES PAR THOB 'GYUR LAS BZHIN NO, ZHES DANG,
record.wylie: de ltar yang bzhi brgya pa las, ,de nyid shes pas gal te 'dir, ,mya ngan 'das pa ma thob kyang, ,skye ba gzhan du 'bad med par, ,nges par thob 'gyur las bzhin no, zhes dang
record.english: The 400 Verses concurs when it says, Once a person has known suchness, Then—even if they fail to attain Nirvana here & now— They are certain to attain it effortlessly Within another life; it's like The case with that kind of karma.

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PAR GSUNGS PA LTAR SNGON DU RANG STENG DU BSAM MO, ,DE NAS SEMS CAN GZHAN LA BSGOM PAR BYA'O,,
record.wylie: bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel par gsungs pa ltar sngon du rang steng du bsam mo, ,de nas sems can gzhan la bsgom par bya'o
record.english: Thus we should do as the commentary to The 400 Verses advises us to: first, contemplate our own situation, and then meditate upon the situation that others find themselves in.

record.acip: YID 'ONG THABS GANG GIS SKYED PA LA MKHAS PA'I DBANG PO DAG GI LUGS GNYIS SNANG BA'I DANG PO NI, ZLA BA'I ZHABS KYIS BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PAR SEMS CAN RNAMS THOG MA MED PA NAS, PHA MA SOGS KYI GNYEN YIN PA BSAMS NA, DE RNAMS BSGRAL BA'I PHYIR DU 'KHOR BAR MCHONG PAR BZOD PA YIN PAR GSUNGS PA LTAR,
record.wylie: yid 'ong thabs gang gis skyed pa la mkhas pa'i dbang po dag gi lugs gnyis snang ba'i dang po ni, zla ba'i zhabs kyis bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel par sems can rnams thog ma med pa nas, pha ma sogs kyi gnyen yin pa bsams na, de rnams bsgral ba'i phyir du 'khor bar mchong par bzod pa yin par gsungs pa ltar
record.english: How do we reach this point, where everyone strikes us as beloved? We see two methods for this described by the Lords of Sages. With the first, we refer to the commentary on The 400 Verses composed by the great Chandrakirti. Here we are instructed to contemplate how—over the length of time with no beginning—each & every living being has been our own father, or mother, or other family or friend. And then we would be willing to throw ourselves into the cycle, in order to free them.

record.acip: DE LTAR MCHOD PAR BRJOD NAS BRTZAM PAR DAM BCA' BA DNGOS SU MA MDZAD KYANG SKYON MED DE, DBU MA RTZA BA DANG RIGS PA DRUG CU PA BZHIN NO,,
record.wylie: de ltar mchod par brjod nas brtsam par dam bca' ba dngos su ma mdzad kyang skyon med de, dbu ma rtsa ba dang rigs pa drug cu pa bzhin no
record.english: It's not a problem that our author here makes the traditional offering of praise but then undertakes no direct commitment to compose the work afterwards, as can also be traditional. We can point to similar examples with the foundational verses of Wisdom, and the Sixty Verses as well.

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PAR YANG ZAB PA DANG RGYA CHE BA'I LAM GYI LUS GSUNGS LA, DBU MA SNYING PO DANG, DBU MA RGYAN DANG, DBU MA'I SGOM RIM GSUM LAS BSDUS TE GSUNGS PA'I LUS RNAMS KYANG 'DRA BAS, 'PHAGS PA'I LUGS 'DZIN PA'I CHEN PO THAMS CAD LAM GYI KHOG LA 'DRA'O,,
record.wylie: bzhi brgya par yang zab pa dang rgya che ba'i lam gyi lus gsungs la, dbu ma snying po dang, dbu ma rgyan dang, dbu ma'i sgom rim gsum las bsdus te gsungs pa'i lus rnams kyang 'dra bas, 'phags pa'i lugs 'dzin pa'i chen po thams cad lam gyi khog la 'dra'o
record.english: The paths of both the profound and the widespread sides of the teaching are also recounted in The 400 Verses. The content of the briefer presentations of them found in three works—The Heart of the Middle Way, The Jewel of the Middle Way, and The Steps of Meditation on the Middle Way—is also similar; and so we can say that the general shape of the path painted by the great upholders of the system of the Realized Being is always the same.

record.acip: 'DI NI MDO KUN LAS BTUS LAS, DAD PA'I RJES SU 'BRANG BA 'JIG RTEN GYI KHAMS THAMS CAD KYI RDUL PHRA RAB KYI RDUL SNYED LA, BSKAL PA GANG+G'A'I KLUNG GI BYE MA SNYED DU, NYI MA RE RE ZHING LHA'I ZAS RO BRGYA PA DANG, LHA'I GOS BYIN PA BAS,
record.wylie: 'di ni mdo kun las btus las, dad pa'i rjes su 'brang ba 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi rdul phra rab kyi rdul snyed la, bskal pa gang+gA'i klung gi bye ma snyed du, nyi ma re re zhing lha'i zas ro brgya pa dang, lha'i gos byin pa bas
record.english: This position in fact accords with that found in the Compendium of All the Sutras, where it speaks of a practitioner who is following after faith, and who—every single day, for the length of eons equal in number to the drops of water found in the Ganges River—presents living beings, equal themselves in number to the particles of dust that compose every planet that exists, with delectable feasts of the gods, and silk of the gods.

record.acip: SHER PHYIN NYIS STONG LNGA BRGYA PA LAS, JI LTAR SHES SHE NA, MA BYUNG BA DANG YANG DAG PAR MA BYUNG BA DANG, LOG PA DANG, DE DAG JI LTAR BYIS PA SO SO'I SKYE BOS BTAGS PA MA YIN PA DANG, JI LTAR BYIS PA SO SO SKYE BOS RNYED PA DE LTAR MA YIN PAR TE, DE'I PHYIR BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' ZHES BYA'O,
record.wylie: sher phyin nyis stong lnga brgya pa las, ji ltar shes she na, ma byung ba dang yang dag par ma byung ba dang, log pa dang, de dag ji ltar byis pa so so'i skye bos btags pa ma yin pa dang, ji ltar byis pa so so skye bos rnyed pa de ltar ma yin par te, de'i phyir byang chub sems dpa' zhes bya'o
record.english: The Perfection of Wisdom in 2500 Lines includes a section that says, How then are we to understand this? The very reason that we call someone a “bodhisattva” is because they never started; they never started at all; they are the total opposite; they are nothing that the infants, the normal beings, think they are; they are nothing at all like the way that these beings, these infants, find them to be.

record.acip: 'DI NI RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS, ,GNAS DANG BCAS PA'I SEMS LDAN LA, ,NYON MONGS DUG CHEN CIS MI 'BYUNG, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA'I DON NO,,
record.wylie: 'di ni rigs pa drug cu pa las, ,gnas dang bcas pa'i sems ldan la, ,nyon mongs dug chen cis mi 'byung, ,zhes gsungs pa'i don no
record.english: This is also the point being made in The Sixty Verses on Reasoning where it says, Why wouldn't the great venom Of the negative emotions Rise within a person Who possesses a state of mind With an opportunity?

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PAR DRANGS PA'I THEG DMAN GYI MDO LAS, GANG SDUG BSNGAL 'DI MA LUS PAR SPANGS PA, NGES PAR SPANGS PA, BYANG BAR GYUR PA, ZAD PA 'DOD CHAGS DANG BRAL BA, 'GOG PA, NYE BAR ZHI BA, NUB PA, SDUG BSNGAL GZHAN GYI MTSAMS MI SBYOR ZHING, MI 'BYUNG MI SKYE BA 'DI NI ZHI BA, 'DI NI GYA NOM PA STE,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel par drangs pa'i theg dman gyi mdo las, gang sdug bsngal 'di ma lus par spangs pa, nges par spangs pa, byang bar gyur pa, zad pa 'dod chags dang bral ba, 'gog pa, nye bar zhi ba, nub pa, sdug bsngal gzhan gyi mtshams mi sbyor zhing, mi 'byung mi skye ba 'di ni zhi ba, 'di ni gya nom pa ste
record.english: We see the following sutra of the lower way quoted in A Commentary to the “Sixty Verses on Reasoning”: Anytime someone is able to eliminate every bit of this suffering; to rid themselves of it forever; to clean it away; to reach the end, free of all desire; to finish it; to put it to a final rest; to see it melt away; never to cross over into more of this suffering; never to see it come again, never to see it rise again—this then is peace, this then is beauty.

record.acip: CES GSUNGS PA 'DIS KYANG THEG DMAN GYI MDO LAS MTHA' GNYIS BKAG PA GSUNGS PAR STON TE, MDO 'DI NI LUNG PHRAN TSEGS NA SNANG NGO, ,DE DAG KYANG MTSON PA TZAM YIN GYI, RIN CHEN PHRENG BA NA 'DIR MA DRANGS PA DU MA ZHIG DANG, RIGS PA DRUG CU PA DANG, BSTOD PA'I TSOGS LAS KYANG DU MA ZHIG GSUNGS SO,,
record.wylie: ces gsungs pa 'dis kyang theg dman gyi mdo las mtha' gnyis bkag pa gsungs par ston te, mdo 'di ni lung phran tshegs na snang ngo, ,de dag kyang mtshon pa tsam yin gyi, rin chen phreng ba na 'dir ma drangs pa du ma zhig dang, rigs pa drug cu pa dang, bstod pa'i tshogs las kyang du ma zhig gsungs so
record.english: These lines are also expressing how sutras of the lower way state that both extremes should be denied—and this particular sutra citation appears in The Assorted Topics of the Word. These are all just representative examples; there are many other supporting citations from the String of Precious Jewels that we have not quoted here—as well as many others from the Sixty Verses on Reasoning, and the Collection of Praises. Refuting arguments covered in the autocommentary

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, BKRA SHIS MA GANG DU ZHUGS PA'I KHYIM DU RNA NAG MA YANG GDON MI ZA BAR YOD DO, ,ZHES GSUNGS PA DANG 'DIR BSHAD PA GNYIS MI 'GAL TE, DER NI MING DE DANG LDAN PA'I GANG ZAG GNYIS LA DGONGS LA, 'DIR NI RNA NAG MA ZHES PA BKRA MI SHIS PA'I MING YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, bkra shis ma gang du zhugs pa'i khyim du rna nag ma yang gdon mi za bar yod do, ,zhes gsungs pa dang 'dir bshad pa gnyis mi 'gal te, der ni ming de dang ldan pa'i gang zag gnyis la dgongs la, 'dir ni rna nag ma zhes pa bkra mi shis pa'i ming yin pa'i phyir ro
record.english: Now it is true that the commentary to The 400 Verses says that “You will find Ill-Starred in the home where Auspicious lives—there is no doubt about it.” There is no contradiction though between this and what we've just described. And this is because that text is intended to refer to two people whose names are “Ill-Starred” and “Auspicious”; whereas in this case “ill-starred” is just another name for “inauspicious.” Two kinds of ethics

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PA LAS KYANG, MYANG 'DAS DON DAM BDEN PA DANG, BDEN PA GZHAN GSUM KUN RDZOB BDEN PAR GSUNGS TE MYANG 'DAS NI 'GOG BDEN NO,,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel pa las kyang, myang 'das don dam bden pa dang, bden pa gzhan gsum kun rdzob bden par gsungs te myang 'das ni 'gog bden no
record.english: The commentary to the Sixty Verses on Reasoning states as well that nirvana is ultimate reality, while the other three truths are deceptive reality; and nirvana consists of the truth of the end of pain.

record.acip: GZHAN YANG RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PAR 'GOG BDEN MNGON SUM DU SHES PA STON PAS ZHAL GYIS BZHES LA, DNGOS POR SMRA BA MNGON SUM TSAD MA DNGOS PO RANG MTSAN GYI YUL CAN DU 'DOD PA LA DE MI RUNG BA DANG,
record.wylie: gzhan yang rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel par 'gog bden mngon sum du shes pa ston pas zhal gyis bzhes la, dngos por smra ba mngon sum tshad ma dngos po rang mtshan gyi yul can du 'dod pa la de mi rung ba dang
record.english: Moreover, this same commentary to the Sixty Verses states that the Teacher held the position that the truth of the end of suffering could be perceived directly; whereas the schools which say that functional things truly exist assert that direct forms of accurate perception can only take, as their object, things which are expressions of archetypes—and so for them, this would be incorrect.

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PA'I, ,GCIG NI NGAN 'GRO NYID 'GRO LA, ,THA MAL MA YIN ZHI NYID DU'O,,
record.wylie: bzhi brgya pa'i, ,gcig ni ngan 'gro nyid 'gro la, ,tha mal ma yin zhi nyid du'o
record.english: The 400 Verses includes these lines: One of them goes no further Than the realms of misery; But the one who is extraordinary Goes nowhere else but peace.

record.acip: DE YANG BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, RANG BZHIN STONG PA NYID KYI GTAM LA GUS PAR 'GYUR NA DE DE DANG MTHUN PA'I RKYEN NYE BAR BSGRUBS PA'I SGO NAS, JI LTAR STONG PA NYID LA DANG BA 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR BA DE LTAR BYA ZHING, SNYING RJE CHE BA DANG, BCOM LDAN 'DAS DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA LA BYAS PA GZO ZHING,
record.wylie: de yang bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, rang bzhin stong pa nyid kyi gtam la gus par 'gyur na de de dang mthun pa'i rkyen nye bar bsgrubs pa'i sgo nas, ji ltar stong pa nyid la dang ba 'phel bar 'gyur ba de ltar bya zhing, snying rje che ba dang, bcom ldan 'das de bzhin gshegs pa la byas pa gzo zhing
record.english: As the commentary to the The 400 Verses puts it, Those who feel respect for discussions of the fact that things are empty of any nature of their own should accomplish the various causes that help bring about these discussions. As your faith in emptiness grows, you should do this more & more, and also work to develop great compassion ever further. You should in addition work to repay the kindness of the Victors—Those Who Have Gone That Way.

record.acip: BDEN 'DZIN DE LAS BYUNG BA'I PHYIR BDEN 'DZIN DES BDEN PAR YOD PA LTAR NYE BAR BSTAN PA MTHONG BA NI RTOG PA YIN GYI DBANG SHES MIN TE, BDEN GNYIS KYI 'GREL PAR DGAG BYA BDEN PA DBANG SHES LA MI SNANG BAR BSHAD PA 'DIR YANG 'DRA BA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: bden 'dzin de las byung ba'i phyir bden 'dzin des bden par yod pa ltar nye bar bstan pa mthong ba ni rtog pa yin gyi dbang shes min te, bden gnyis kyi 'grel par dgag bya bden pa dbang shes la mi snang bar bshad pa 'dir yang 'dra ba'i phyir ro
record.english: “Because they come from this place” means a place where we are grasping onto things as being real; and this tendency of holding on to things as real sees what is presented to us as though it existed in truth. This “seeing” by the way is actually just having an idea, and is not referring to a sense consciousness. And that's because the case here is similar to that described in the Commentary to the Two Realities, where it says that the thing we deny—“real” existence—is not something which could ever appear to a sense consciousness.

record.acip: SROG CHAGS DE DAG GI BSAM PA NI RTOG PA KHO NA MIN GYI, RTOG MED KYI SHES PA LA YANG BYA STE, DE GNYIS KYI DBANG GIS YOD PAR BZHAG PA'I DON DAM PAR YOD PA MIN PA'I DNGOS PO BRDZUN PA RNAMS KUN RDZOB KHO NAR YOD PA NI, DNGOS RNAMS SKYE BA KUN RDZOB TU, ZHES PA'I DON TE, DE YANG BDEN 'DZIN GYI KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA'I DON MIN NO,,
record.wylie: srog chags de dag gi bsam pa ni rtog pa kho na min gyi, rtog med kyi shes pa la yang bya ste, de gnyis kyi dbang gis yod par bzhag pa'i don dam par yod pa min pa'i dngos po brdzun pa rnams kun rdzob kho nar yod pa ni, dngos rnams skye ba kun rdzob tu, zhes pa'i don te, de yang bden 'dzin gyi kun rdzob tu yod pa'i don min no
record.english: Now it's not the case that every thought that these living creatures ever have is discursive; rather, this description also applies to the thoughts they have which are not. The things though that these two establish as existing and which lie to us—that is, things which are not such that they exist as the ultimate—can only exist deceptively. This is the point of the lines quoted, where they say that “everything in the world starts in a way which is deceptive.” This is not, by the way, to say that all these things are deceptive in the sense of being the tendency to take things as real.

record.acip: GNYIS PA NI, LUGS 'DI LA CHOS RNAMS RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PA TZAM GYI 'JOG TSUL SHES NA, DE LAS BZLOG STE 'DZIN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN BDE BLAG TU SHES PAR 'GYUR BAS,
record.wylie: gnyis pa ni, lugs 'di la chos rnams rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag pa tsam gyi 'jog tshul shes na, de las bzlog ste 'dzin pa'i bden 'dzin bde blag tu shes par 'gyur bas
record.english: This brings us to our second step from above, which is how the system of the Consequence section of the Middle Way school identifies the way in which we hold on to things as being real. Now if you understand how this system says that things are established simply by force of ideas, then you will with ease understand what it is to hold that things exist the opposite way: to hold things as “real.”

record.acip: 'DI LA GNYIS, CHOS RNAMS RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS 'JOG TSUL DANG, DE LAS BZLOG STE 'DZIN PA'I BDEN 'DZIN BSTAN PA'O,,
record.wylie: 'di la gnyis, chos rnams rtog pa'i dbang gis 'jog tshul dang, de las bzlog ste 'dzin pa'i bden 'dzin bstan pa'o
record.english: We'll proceed then in two parts: how it is that things are established by force of ideas; followed by a presentation of what it is to hold things as real: as the opposite of something created by ideas. Things are creations of thoughts

record.acip: DANG PO NI, NYE BAR 'KHOR GYIS ZHUS PA LAS, ,SNA TSOGS YID DGA' ME TOG KHA BYE ZHING, ,GSER GYI KHANG MCHOG 'BAR BA YID 'ONG BA, ,'DI NA DE LA'ANG BYED PA 'GA' MED DE, ,DE DAG RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PA YIN, ,RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS 'JIG RTEN RNAM BRTAGS TE,
record.wylie: dang po ni, nye bar 'khor gyis zhus pa las, ,sna tshogs yid dga' me tog kha bye zhing, ,gser gyi khang mchog 'bar ba yid 'ong ba, ,'di na de la'ang byed pa 'ga' med de, ,de dag rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag pa yin, ,rtog pa'i dbang gis 'jig rten rnam brtags te
record.english: Here is the first; we begin with lines from The Sutra Requested by Upali: Flowers break open In a rainbow of pleasing colors; Perfect palaces of pure gold Blaze in lovely light. But there was no creator Who crafted any of it— They are all creations Of thoughts; The world is all made up By our thoughts.

record.acip: ZHES CHOS RNAMS RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PAR GSUNGS TE, CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DANG RTOG PA'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PAR GSUNGS PA GZHAN YANG MANG NGO,,
record.wylie: zhes chos rnams rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag par gsungs te, chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa tsam dang rtog pa'i dbang gis bzhag par gsungs pa gzhan yang mang ngo
record.english: What this is saying is that all the things in the universe are creations of our thoughts—and there are many other statements in scripture that describe how none of these things are anything but projections of our thoughts: creations of our thoughts.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,'JIG RTEN MA RIG RKYEN CAN DU, ,GANG PHYIR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSUNGS, ,DE YI PHYIR NA 'JIG RTEN 'DI, ,RNAM RTOG YIN ZHES CIS MI 'THAD,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,'jig rten ma rig rkyen can du, ,gang phyir rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gsungs, ,de yi phyir na 'jig rten 'di, ,rnam rtog yin zhes cis mi 'thad
record.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning say as well: The totally enlightened Buddha Himself has stated that this world Was born from misunderstanding. Why then would it be An overstatement to say That the world is just Our imagination?

record.acip: CES GSUNGS PA'I DON 'GREL PAR 'JIG RTEN RNAMS RANG GI NGO BOS MA GRUB PA RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DU BSHAD CING, BRGYA PA LAS KYANG,
record.wylie: ces gsungs pa'i don 'grel par 'jig rten rnams rang gi ngo bos ma grub pa rtog pas btags pa tsam du bshad cing, brgya pa las kyang
record.english: The commentary explains these lines as meaning that the various worlds which exist are simply creations of thoughts; none of them exists through any nature of its own. The 400 Verses says as well:

record.acip: ,RTOG PA MED PAR 'DOD CHAGS LA, ,SOGS LA YOD NYID YOD MIN NA, ,YANG DAG DON DANG RTOG PA ZHES, ,BLO DANG LDAN PA SU ZHIG 'DZIN,
record.wylie: rtog pa med par 'dod chags la, ,sogs la yod nyid yod min na, ,yang dag don dang rtog pa zhes, ,blo dang ldan pa su zhig 'dzin
record.english: Without thoughts It would be impossible For desire & the rest To exist at all. Who then With a brain in their head Could ever speak Of something pure, Or of thought that's pure?

record.acip: ZHES GSUNGS SHING DE'I 'GREL PA LAS KYANG, RTOG PA YOD PA KHO NAS YOD PA NYID DANG, RTOG PA MED PAR YOD PA NYID MED PA DE DAG NI, GOR MA CHAG PAR THAG PA BSDOGS PA LA BTAGS PA'I SBRUL LTAR RANG GI NGO BOS MA GRUB PAR NGES SO, ZHES GSUNGS TE YANG DAG DON NI RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA'O, ,RTOG PA NI DE LA BLTOS TE SKYE BA'O,,
record.wylie: zhes gsungs shing de'i 'grel pa las kyang, rtog pa yod pa kho nas yod pa nyid dang, rtog pa med par yod pa nyid med pa de dag ni, gor ma chag par thag pa bsdogs pa la btags pa'i sbrul ltar rang gi ngo bos ma grub par nges so, zhes gsungs te yang dag don ni rang gi ngo bos grub pa'o, ,rtog pa ni de la bltos te skye ba'o
record.english: The commentary to the same work says that Existence itself can exist only through thought; and non-existence itself only through an absence of thought. It is certain, beyond any question, that neither of these can exist through any nature of its own: they are ropes called “snakes.”

record.acip: DE LTAR CHOS RNAMS KYI NGO BO YUL CAN THA SNYAD KYI RTOG PA GZHAN LA RAG MA LAS PA STE, DE'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PA MIN PA'I RANG BZHIN DE NYID LA DGAG BYA'I BDAG CES BYA LA,
record.wylie: de ltar chos rnams kyi ngo bo yul can tha snyad kyi rtog pa gzhan la rag ma las pa ste, de'i dbang gis bzhag pa min pa'i rang bzhin de nyid la dgag bya'i bdag ces bya la
record.english: As such, an essential nature of existing things would be something that does not rely upon some other, subject state of mind which is a nominal perception. And so what we call the “self” in terms of being what emptiness denies is precisely this kind of self-nature: one which does not require being established by force of such a perception.

record.acip: RANG BZHIN DE GANG ZAG DANG CHOS KYI STENG DU YOD PAR 'DZIN PA NI BDAG GNYIS KYI 'DZIN PAR SHUGS KYIS RTOGS TE, BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, DE LA BDAG CES BYA BA NI GANG ZHIG DNGOS PO RNAMS KYI GZHAN LA RAG MA LAS PA'I NGO BO RANG BZHIN TE, DE MED PA NI BDAG MED PA'O, , DE NI CHOS DANG GANG ZAG GI DBYE BAS GNYIS SU RTOGS TE, CHOS KYI BDAG MED PA DANG GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PA ZHES BYA'O, ZHES PA LTAR STE,
record.wylie: rang bzhin de gang zag dang chos kyi steng du yod par 'dzin pa ni bdag gnyis kyi 'dzin par shugs kyis rtogs te, brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, de la bdag ces bya ba ni gang zhig dngos po rnams kyi gzhan la rag ma las pa'i ngo bo rang bzhin te, de med pa ni bdag med pa'o, , de ni chos dang gang zag gi dbye bas gnyis su rtogs te, chos kyi bdag med pa dang gang zag gi bdag med pa zhes bya'o, zhes pa ltar ste
record.english: We can then understand, by implication, that to hold that this kind of nature could in fact apply to a person or to things is what it is to “believe in the two kinds of a self-nature.” As the commentary to the 400 Verses puts it, When we say “self-nature,” what we're talking about is some essence or nature where entities could not rely upon other things. The general absence of this is what we call the “lack of a self-nature.” Understand that this comes in two versions: that which applies to things, and that which applies to people. Which is to say, we speak of the “lack of a self-nature to things,” and the “lack of a self-nature to people.”

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PA LAS KYANG, ,YUL LA BDAG MED MTHONG NA NI, ,SRID PA'I SA BON 'GAG PAR 'GYUR, ZHES DANG,
record.wylie: bzhi brgya pa las kyang, ,yul la bdag med mthong na ni, ,srid pa'i sa bon 'gag par 'gyur, zhes dang
record.english: The 400 Verses also states: Once we see in things That they have no nature Of their own, The seeds for suffering life Come to a stop.

record.acip: BDEN 'DZIN DE 'JUG 'GREL DANG, BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA GNYIS KAR NYON MONGS CAN GYI MA RIG PAR BSHAD LA, MA RIG PA DE NYAN RANG DGRA BCOM GYIS SPANGS PA DANG, BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PAR MI SKYE BA'I CHOS LA BZOD PA THOB PA'I BYANG SEMS KYIS SPANGS PAR BSHAD DO,,
record.wylie: bden 'dzin de 'jug 'grel dang, bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa gnyis kar nyon mongs can gyi ma rig par bshad la, ma rig pa de nyan rang dgra bcom gyis spangs pa dang, bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel par mi skye ba'i chos la bzod pa thob pa'i byang sems kyis spangs par bshad do
record.english: The tendency to believe that things are real is explained—in both the autocommentary to Entering the Middle Way and in the commentary to the 400 Verses—to be misunderstanding which is involved with negative emotions. Listener and self-made buddha types of enemy destroyers have rid themselves of that form of misunderstanding; and the commentary to the 400 Verses explains that a bodhisattva who has attained the state called “mastery over unborn things” has as well rid themselves of this misunderstanding.

record.acip: 'DOD CHAGS LA SOGS PA NYON MONGS GZHAN RNAMS KYANG BDEN 'DZIN GYI GTI MUG LAS 'JUG TSUL NI, BZHI BRGYA PA LAS, ,LUS LA LUS DBANG JI BZHIN DU, ,GTI MUG KUN LA GNAS 'GYUR TE,
record.wylie: 'dod chags la sogs pa nyon mongs gzhan rnams kyang bden 'dzin gyi gti mug las 'jug tshul ni, bzhi brgya pa las, ,lus la lus dbang ji bzhin du, ,gti mug kun la gnas 'gyur te
record.english: How do we describe the way in which desire & the rest—the other negative emotions—engage in their objects by way of that dark ignorance where we still hold that things are real? As the 400 Verses puts it, Dark ignorance abides In all of them, Just as the powers of the body Reside throughout it.

record.acip: DNGOS PO BDEN 'DZIN 'DI NI 'KHOR BA'I RTZA BA'I MA RIG PAR YANG STONG NYID BDUN CU PA LAS GSUNGS SHING, RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,GANG YANG RUNG BA'I GNAS RNYED NA, ,NYON MONGS SBRUL GDUG G-YO CAN GYIS, ,ZIN PAR 'GYUR RO GANG GI SEMS, ,GNAS MED DE DAG ZIN MI 'GYUR,
record.wylie: dngos po bden 'dzin 'di ni 'khor ba'i rtsa ba'i ma rig par yang stong nyid bdun cu pa las gsungs shing, rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,gang yang rung ba'i gnas rnyed na, ,nyon mongs sbrul gdug g-yo can gyis, ,zin par 'gyur ro gang gi sems, ,gnas med de dag zin mi 'gyur
record.english: The Seventy Verses also states that this tendency of holding things to be real constitutes the misunderstanding which is the root of the cycle of pain. And the Sixty Verses says as well, If some opportunity Or another is found, Then the deadly, devious viper Of the negative emotions Will catch us. Those who never go To this place Will never be caught.

record.acip: DON 'DI NYID MDO DE NYID LAS, ,'DU BYED RNAMS NI MA RIG RKYEN CAN TE, ,'DU BYED DE DAG DE NYID DU YOD MIN, ,'DU BYED MA RIG 'DI GNYIS STONG PA STE, ,RANG BZHIN GYIS NI G-YO BA DANG BRAL BA, ZHES BYA BAS BSHAD DE,
record.wylie: don 'di nyid mdo de nyid las, ,'du byed rnams ni ma rig rkyen can te, ,'du byed de dag de nyid du yod min, ,'du byed ma rig 'di gnyis stong pa ste, ,rang bzhin gyis ni g-yo ba dang bral ba, zhes bya bas bshad de
record.english: This point is clarified in the same sutra, in the following words— Incidents of fresh karma Are things that have Misunderstanding as their cause; These cases of fresh karma Are not something that exist In and of themselves. Fresh karmas and misunderstanding, These two, are empty; They are free of any shifting Through any nature of their own.

record.acip: BRGYA PA LAS, ,STONG MIN STONG LDAN MTHONG MIN TE, ,MYANG 'DAS BDAG GIR GYUR CIG CES, ,LOG LTAS MYA NGAN MI 'DA' BAR, ,DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS KYIS GSUNGS, ZHES DANG,
record.wylie: brgya pa las, ,stong min stong ldan mthong min te, ,myang 'das bdag gir gyur cig ces, ,log ltas mya ngan mi 'da' bar, ,de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyis gsungs, zhes dang
record.english: As The Hundred puts it, Its not as though we see Something that's not empty As having emptiness; For Those Gone Thus Have stated that The statement that “I've made nirvana my own” Is a wrong view which means You have not reached nirvana.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PA LAS KYANG, 'DUS BYAS LOG PAR SNANG NAS BYIS PA SLU BAR BYED PA BZHIN DU, MYANG 'DAS DON DAM PAS DE LTAR SNANG NAS MI SLU BAS MYANG 'DAS BDEN PA DANG, GZHAN RNAMS MI BDEN PAR GSUNGS PAR BSHAD PAS, BDEN MI BDEN GNYIS SU PHYE BA NI SLU MI SLU'I DON YIN PAR GDON MI ZA BAR 'DOD PAR BYA'O,,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel pa las kyang, 'dus byas log par snang nas byis pa slu bar byed pa bzhin du, myang 'das don dam pas de ltar snang nas mi slu bas myang 'das bden pa dang, gzhan rnams mi bden par gsungs par bshad pas, bden mi bden gnyis su phye ba ni slu mi slu'i don yin par gdon mi za bar 'dod par bya'o
record.english: The commentary to the Sixty Verses describes how composed things appear in a wrong way and deceive infants; whereas—since nirvana is ultimate—it does not appear in this way, and does not deceive. As such then, nirvana is described as being real, and the others as not being real. We can thus say that the position being taken here is that the division into two realities is being made according to whether or not things are deceiving us.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PA LAS MYANG 'DAS KUN RDZOB TU BDEN PAR GSUNGS PA NI, MYANG 'DAS DON DAM PA'I BDEN PAR YOD PA KUN RDZOB PA'I NGOR 'JOG PA'I DON YIN GYI, THA SNYAD DU DE BDEN PAR BZHED PA MIN NO,,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel pa las myang 'das kun rdzob tu bden par gsungs pa ni, myang 'das don dam pa'i bden par yod pa kun rdzob pa'i ngor 'jog pa'i don yin gyi, tha snyad du de bden par bzhed pa min no
record.english: When the commentary to the Sixty Verses says that nirvana is, in a deceptive way, real, what it means is that—to deceptive perceptions—nirvana is established as existing as reality which is ultimate. The work is not though saying that, in nominal terms, that is being accepted as real.

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PAR SLOB DPON CHOS SKYONG GIS BZHI BRGYA PA'I LTA BA SEMS TZAM DU BKRAL BAR BSHAD PAS DE LA SBYAR NA 'GRIG GO
record.wylie: bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel par slob dpon chos skyong gis bzhi brgya pa'i lta ba sems tsam du bkral bar bshad pas de la sbyar na 'grig go
record.english: In his commentary to the 400 Verses, Master Dharmapala explains the viewpoints of the 400 as commenting upon the Mind Only school; and it would seem acceptable to apply that here.

record.acip: BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, DNGOS PO DNGOS PO YOD PAR SMRA BA'I LTAR NA NI JI SRID DU DNGOS PO DE'I YOD PA NYID YIN PA DE SRID DU, DE LTAR RANG GI NGO BO YANG YIN PA NYID LA, GANG GI TSE RANG GI NGO BO DANG BRAL BA DE'I TSE DE LA DNGOS PO DE RNAM PA THAMS CAD DU MED PA'I PHYIR, BONG BU'I RVA DANG 'DRA BAS GNYIS SU SMRA BA LAS MA 'DAS PA'I PHYIR, 'DI'I MNGON PAR 'DOD PA THAMS CAD 'GRIG DKA' BAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES SO,,
record.wylie: brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, dngos po dngos po yod par smra ba'i ltar na ni ji srid du dngos po de'i yod pa nyid yin pa de srid du, de ltar rang gi ngo bo yang yin pa nyid la, gang gi tshe rang gi ngo bo dang bral ba de'i tshe de la dngos po de rnam pa thams cad du med pa'i phyir, bong bu'i rva dang 'dra bas gnyis su smra ba las ma 'das pa'i phyir, 'di'i mngon par 'dod pa thams cad 'grig dka' bar 'gyur ro, zhes so
record.english: The commentary to The Hundred puts it this way— According to those who say that things exist, the essential nature of a thing is also there, just as long as the existence of that same thing is there; and at any point where that same thing loses its essential nature, then the thing itself can no longer exist in any form at all: it becomes the exact equivalent of a rabbit horn. As long as they think this way, then these people are never anything more than those who assert a discrepancy. As such, it is quite difficult to reconcile all the beliefs that people like this hold.

record.acip: LAN DU, LAS BYAS PA'I SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR 'GAGS ZIN PA'I SNGA LOGS KYI LAS 'GAG PA LA MNGON DU PHYOGS PA'I TSE, LAS KYI NUS PA GZHAG PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR KHA CIG KUN GZHI RNAM PAR SHES PA RTOG PAR BYED LA, KHA CIG BU LON GYI DBANG RGYA STE DE'I YI GE DANG 'DRA BA'I LAS GNYIS LAS DON GZHAN PA, CHUD MI ZA BA ZHES PA LDAN MIN 'DU BYED DU GYUR PA CIG 'DOD DO,,
record.wylie: lan du, las byas pa'i skad cig gnyis par 'gags zin pa'i snga logs kyi las 'gag pa la mngon du phyogs pa'i tshe, las kyi nus pa gzhag par bya ba'i phyir kha cig kun gzhi rnam par shes pa rtog par byed la, kha cig bu lon gyi dbang rgya ste de'i yi ge dang 'dra ba'i las gnyis las don gzhan pa, chud mi za ba zhes pa ldan min 'du byed du gyur pa cig 'dod do
record.english: In response to this, some people point to the karma which is approaching stopping: that karma just previous to the point at which the karma has stopped, in the second instant of the commission of the karma. In this moment, they say, there must be a place where the potential of the karma is deposited; and so it is that some people imagine that there must be a type of awareness known as “foundation consciousness.” And there are also some who say that there is some other entity, distinct from the two karmas, similar to a letter of credit or receipt for a loan; something—a separate changing entity that is neither physical nor mental—which consists of the fact that the karma will never just fade away.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,RGYU ZAD NYID LAS ZHI BA NI, ,ZAD CES BYA BAR DMIGS PA STE,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,rgyu zad nyid las zhi ba ni, ,zad ces bya bar dmigs pa ste
record.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning says, as well, We observe what we call The wearing out, Or coming to a rest, From the simple wearing out Of the cause.

record.acip: RIM PA DE LTAR BYA BA LA DGONGS NAS BRGYA PA LAS, ,GANG ZHIG GANG GANG LA DGA' BA, ,DE YI DE DE SNGAR SPYAD BYA, ,NYAMS PAR GYUR PA DAM CHOS KYI, ,SNOD NI CIS KYANG MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
record.wylie: rim pa de ltar bya ba la dgongs nas brgya pa las, ,gang zhig gang gang la dga' ba, ,de yi de de sngar spyad bya, ,nyams par gyur pa dam chos kyi, ,snod ni cis kyang ma yin no, zhes gsungs so
record.english: The 400 Verses has this graduated approach in mind when it says, Let people start out doing Whatever it is that they Might first be attracted to; When it fails them, Why then wouldn't they Become worthy vessels For the highest teachings of all?

record.acip: DE'I PHYIR GDON MI ZA BAR PHYI ROL TU 'KHRUL BA'I RTOG PA'I RGYU GZUNG 'DZIN RDZAS THA DAD PA GNYIS SU SNANG BA'I MA DAG GZHAN DBANG KHAS BLANG DGOS TE, SNANG GZHI DE NYID KUN BYANG GI 'CHING GROL GNYIS KA'I RGYU YIN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: de'i phyir gdon mi za bar phyi rol tu 'khrul ba'i rtog pa'i rgyu gzung 'dzin rdzas tha dad pa gnyis su snang ba'i ma dag gzhan dbang khas blang dgos te, snang gzhi de nyid kun byang gi 'ching grol gnyis ka'i rgyu yin pa'i phyir ro
record.english: As such, we must—beyond the slightest doubt—accept the concept of an impure form of dominated entities, where the objects held and the perceptions holding them do appear to be such that to be one is not to be the other; that is, there must be some basis for the mistaken perception that outer objects exist. We can even say that the very scenario which appears to us is the exact cause behind the fetters and the freedom, of vast negativity and perfect enlightenment.

record.acip: TSAD MA PHYI MA GNYIS NI RJES DPAG TU 'DU LA BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS KYANG, DNGOS PO THAMS CAD MNGON SUM DU SHES PAS GO BAR BYA BA NI MA YIN GYI RJES SU DPAG PAS RTOGS PAR BYA BA YANG YOD DO, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
record.wylie: tshad ma phyi ma gnyis ni rjes dpag tu 'du la bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa las kyang, dngos po thams cad mngon sum du shes pas go bar bya ba ni ma yin gyi rjes su dpag pas rtogs par bya ba yang yod do, zhes gsungs so
record.english: The latter two types of accurate perception can be grouped into the deductive form of this perception; and as the commentary to the 400 Verses puts it, “Not all entities are such that they can be grasped by direct forms of perception; there are also those which must be perceived through the deductive form.”

record.acip: BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, CHOS MNGON PA NAS GZUGS SOGS LNGA RE RE ZHING DBANG PO DANG YID SHES KYIS SHES PAR BYA BAR GSUNGS PA'I DON 'CHAD PA NA, RNAM PAR SHES PA GNYIS KYIS DON GCIG RNAM PAR SHES PA MA YIN TE, GCIG NI YUL GYI RNAM PA DNGOS SU GCOD PAR BYED PA STE GANG DANG POR SKYE BA'O,,
record.wylie: bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, chos mngon pa nas gzugs sogs lnga re re zhing dbang po dang yid shes kyis shes par bya bar gsungs pa'i don 'chad pa na, rnam par shes pa gnyis kyis don gcig rnam par shes pa ma yin te, gcig ni yul gyi rnam pa dngos su gcod par byed pa ste gang dang por skye ba'o
record.english: The commentary to The 400 Verses has a section where it is giving an explanation of the part in the works on higher knowledge which refer to each of the five of form and the rest; the sense powers; and what is perceived by the consciousness of the thought. Here it says that it is not the case that two kinds of consciousness can be aware of a single object—because one of them will directly discern the aspect of the object; and this will be the first to arise. Rejecting rebuttal on another consciousness

record.acip: YANG BZHI BRGYA PA'I 'GREL PA LAS, TSOR BA LA SOGS PA LTAR NYAMS SU MYONG BA'I RNAM PA YANG MA YIN LA, GZUGS DANG SGRA LA SOGS PA BZHIN DBANG PO'I SGO NAS YONGS SU BCAD PAR BYA BA YANG MA YIN NO, ZHES GSUNGS PAS
record.wylie: yang bzhi brgya pa'i 'grel pa las, tshor ba la sogs pa ltar nyams su myong ba'i rnam pa yang ma yin la, gzugs dang sgra la sogs pa bzhin dbang po'i sgo nas yongs su bcad par bya ba yang ma yin no, zhes gsungs pas
record.english: The commentary to the 400 Verses also says, It does not display an aspect of experience which is similar to that of feeling or the like. But then again neither is it similar to the case with things like visible form and sound, where the final discernment is made through the sense power.

record.acip: 'DI NYID 'PHAGS PA LHA YANG BZHED DE BRGYA PA LAS, ,GCIG YOD GCIG MED CES BYA BA, ,DE NYID MIN 'JIG RTEN PA'ANG MIN, ,ZHES DON SHES YOD MED 'BYED PA BDEN GNYIS GANG GI YANG RNAM GZHAG MIN PAR GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: 'di nyid 'phags pa lha yang bzhed de brgya pa las, ,gcig yod gcig med ces bya ba, ,de nyid min 'jig rten pa'ang min, ,zhes don shes yod med 'byed pa bden gnyis gang gi yang rnam gzhag min par gsungs pa'i phyir ro
record.english: This very point is something that Master Aryadeva also agrees to; as the 400 Verses puts it, Saying that one is there, Or that one is not there, Is not with that particular one; Nor with that of the world.

record.acip: ,GAL TE 'DI DAG SEMS TZAM ZHES MKHYEN NAS, ,DE LAS GZUGS NYID DGAG PAR MDZAD NA NI, ,SLAR YANG DE LAS BDAG NYID CHEN POS SEMS, ,GTI MUG LAS LAS SKYES PAR CI PHYIR GSUNGS,
record.wylie: gal te 'di dag sems tsam zhes mkhyen nas, ,de las gzugs nyid dgag par mdzad na ni, ,slar yang de las bdag nyid chen pos sems, ,gti mug las las skyes par ci phyir gsungs
record.english: Suppose all these Were referred to As “only the mind,” And the Buddha Knew this, and so Meant in this To deny “form itself.” And then how Could it be in it For the Great Being To state that the mind Was born from Dark ignorance And karma?

record.acip: KHYOD KYI LUGS LTAR NA GAL TE KHAMS GSUM PO 'DI DAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I SEMS TZAM MO ZHES MKHYEN NAS, SA BCU PA DE LAS PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NYID DGAG PAR MDZAD NA NI,
record.wylie: khyod kyi lugs ltar na gal te khams gsum po 'di dag rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i sems tsam mo zhes mkhyen nas, sa bcu pa de las phyi rol gyi gzugs nyid dgag par mdzad na ni
record.english: Suppose then it were the way that your system would have it. That is, suppose all these three realms of existence were referred to as “only the mind,” as something which existed through its own nature. And suppose the Buddha knew this, and so meant—in this Ten Levels—to deny “form itself,” in the sense of outer form.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,'JIG RTEN MA RIG RKYEN CAN DU, ,GANG PHYIR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSUNG, ,DE YI PHYIR NA 'JIG RTEN 'DI, ,RNAM RTOG YIN ZHES CIS MI 'THAD,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,'jig rten ma rig rkyen can du, ,gang phyir rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gsung, ,de yi phyir na 'jig rten 'di, ,rnam rtog yin zhes cis mi 'thad
record.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning also says it like this— The total Buddhas stated That the world is rooted In misunderstanding. Why then would it ever be Incorrect to say That this entire world Is our imagination?

record.acip: DPER NA SBRUL NI THAG PA BSDOGS PA'I RTEN 'BREL LA LOG PAR BTAGS PA YIN TE SBRUL DE THAG PA DE LA MED PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: dper na sbrul ni thag pa bsdogs pa'i rten 'brel la log par btags pa yin te sbrul de thag pa de la med pa'i phyir ro
record.english: Let's consider for example a case where there is a mistaken appellation, for the connection between a rope and a snake; that is, there is absolutely no snake there amidst the rope.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS, ,DE DANG DE RTEN GANG 'BYUNG BA, ,RANG GI NGO BO DER MA SKYES, ,RANG GI NGO BOR GANG MA SKYES, ,DE NI SKYES ZHES JI SKAD BYA,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las, ,de dang de rten gang 'byung ba, ,rang gi ngo bo der ma skyes, ,rang gi ngo bor gang ma skyes, ,de ni skyes zhes ji skad bya
record.english: As the Sixty Verses on the Reasoning behind Emptiness puts it, Anything which occurs In dependence On any particular thing Cannot have started In & of itself. How could you ever say That something which Had not yet started, In & of itself, Then started?

record.acip: RTZA SHE DANG RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LA SOGS PA GZHUNG DU MAR, 'PHAGS PAS BCOM LDAN 'DAS LA RTEN 'BYUNG GSUNG PA NYID KYI SGO NAS BSTOD PA MDZAD PA LA, BRTEN NAS SKYES PA NYID KYIS MA SKYES SO ZHES PA'I MUN SPRUL GANG CI YANG RUNG BA SHES RAB CAN GYIS SMRA BAR MI BYA'O,,
record.wylie: rtsa she dang rigs pa drug cu pa la sogs pa gzhung du mar, 'phags pas bcom ldan 'das la rten 'byung gsung pa nyid kyi sgo nas bstod pa mdzad pa la, brten nas skyes pa nyid kyis ma skyes so zhes pa'i mun sprul gang ci yang rung ba shes rab can gyis smra bar mi bya'o
record.english: And so too is it that in many great classics such as Wisdom or The Sixty Verses, the Realized Being himself has sung the praises of the Conqueror for this very fact: that he spoke to us of how things occur in dependence. And so too is it that those of you with intelligence should never devolve into some kind of total darkness and say things like “things cannot start, since they must start in dependence.”

record.acip: BRGYA PA LAS KYANG, ,DNGOS RNAMS RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD NA, ,STONG MTHONG YON TAN CI ZHIG YOD, ,RTOG PAS MTHONG BA 'CHING BA STE, ,DE NYID 'DIR NI 'GOG PA YIN,
record.wylie: brgya pa las kyang, ,dngos rnams rang bzhin gyis yod na, ,stong mthong yon tan ci zhig yod, ,rtog pas mthong ba 'ching ba ste, ,de nyid 'dir ni 'gog pa yin
record.english: As the 400 Verses puts it, If things did exist Through some nature Of their own, Then what good Would it ever be To see emptiness? Those who see With their conceptions Are enslaved; And that's exactly What we here deny.

record.acip: BRGYA BA LAS, ,CHOS 'DI DE BZHIN GSHEGS RNAMS KYIS, ,RTZOD PA MDZAD PHYIR GSUNGS MA YIN, ,'ON KYANG ME YIS BUD SHING LTAR, ,'DI YIS PHAS KYI RGOL BA SREG
record.wylie: brgya ba las, ,chos 'di de bzhin gshegs rnams kyis, ,rtsod pa mdzad phyir gsungs ma yin, ,'on kyang me yis bud shing ltar, ,'di yis phas kyi rgol ba sreg
record.english: As the 400 Verses puts it, The teachings were never Granted by Those Gone Thus So that they could engage In simple disputation. But yes they did indeed Incinerate their opponents, Just because that is what Fire tends to do with wood.

record.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,RTZOD MED CHE BA'I BDAG NYID CAN, ,DE DAG LA NI PHYOGS MED DO, ,GANG RNAMS LA NI PHYOGS MED PA, ,DE LA GZHAN PHYOGS GA LA YOD, CES DANG,
record.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,rtsod med che ba'i bdag nyid can, ,de dag la ni phyogs med do, ,gang rnams la ni phyogs med pa, ,de la gzhan phyogs ga la yod, ces dang
record.english: As the Sixty Verses on the Logic of Emptiness puts it, Those who are great beings Take no position, And never engage in dispute. How could there be Some other position, For those who have No position themselves?

record.acip: BRGYA PA LAS KYANG, ,RANG GI PHYOGS LA CHAGS YOD CING, ,GZHAN PHYOGS LA KHYOD MI DGA' NA, ,MYA NGAN 'DAS PAR MI 'GRO STE, ,GNYIS SPYOD ZHI BAR YOD MI 'GYUR, ZHES DANG,
record.wylie: brgya pa las kyang, ,rang gi phyogs la chags yod cing, ,gzhan phyogs la khyod mi dga' na, ,mya ngan 'das par mi 'gro ste, ,gnyis spyod zhi bar yod mi 'gyur, zhes dang
record.english: The 400 Verses says as well, When you have attachment To your own position, And feel unhappy With the positions of others, You will never travel To nirvana. There is no peace For those who live In division.

record.acip: GNYIS PA GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RIGS PAS BSGRUB PA LA GSUM, THAR 'DOD KYIS THOG MAR BDAG RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NYID DGAG DGOS PAR BSTAN PA, BDAG DANG BDAG GI BA GNYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GOG PA'I TSUL, BDAG DANG SHING RTA'I DPYAD PA DNGOS PO GZHAN LA YANG BSGRE BAR BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
record.wylie: gnyis pa gang zag gi bdag med rigs pas bsgrub pa la gsum, thar 'dod kyis thog mar bdag rang bzhin gyis grub pa nyid dgag dgos par bstan pa, bdag dang bdag gi ba gnyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'gog pa'i tshul, bdag dang shing rta'i dpyad pa dngos po gzhan la yang bsgre bar bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
record.english: With this we have reached our second major part from above, on using reasoning to prove that the person has no self-nature. This itself we will cover in three sections: (1) showing how those who wish to achieve freedom need, before anything else, to deny that the self is something that could exist through any nature of its own; (2) how it is that we deny the idea that either me or mine could exist through any nature of their own; and (3) the way in which we can apply our examination of the self, and of a wagon, to other entities as well. Here is the first.

record.acip: DE LTAR MTHONG BA NA 'JIG LTA SPONG BAR 'DOD PA 'BYUNG LA, DE'I TSE SHES RAB CAN ZHIG YIN NA NI DE SPONG BA DE YANG SNGAR CHOS DBYINGS BSTOD PA DANG BZHI BRGYA PA'I LUNG DRANGS PA LTAR 'JIG LTAS JI LTAR BZUNG BA LTAR GYI BDAG YUL STENG NA MED PAR MTHONG BAS SPONG DGOS PAR MTHONG NAS,

record.english: When we do see this fact, then we start to feel a desire to eliminate this view of destruction. At this point, if someone is a person of intelligence, they see what it is that they have to give up to accomplish this. record.english: What this is describing is a point at which we have gained mastery over the wisdom, at the eighth bodhisattva level, where we are no longer imagining any self-existence. record.english: Let's consider then these same twelve groups of high qualities at five different bodhisattva levels: the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and the seventh. record.english: The first of our logical statements above is always true. For suppose that a person is still unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he hold the parts to the person, the thing which gets the label of "me," as existing through some nature of its own. As long as he goes on this way, then he will continue to find himself unable to root out the object that he thinks he sees when he holds the thing which gets the label, the "me," as existing from its own side. And as long as he continues with this, then by the power of this misperception he will continue to collect karma. And as long as he collects karma, then he will continue to spin around in this wheel of suffering life.

record.english: And this is true first of all because the Perfect Explanation, an Illumination of the True Thought, states that—when the commentary to the Sixty Verses of Reasoning describes nirvana as deceptive reality—what it means is that nirvana must be established as existing as ultimate reality with reference toa deceived state of mind. record.english: And the list goes on and on. The point is that—if something occurs in dependence upon causes and conditions, or upon its parts—then it is something which has occurred under the control of other forces: it has occurred because of its reliance upon other things. It is not though something which has come about on its own power, or without relying on something else; and as such, it does not exist through some nature of its own. As the 400 Verses puts it:

record.english: The logic we have outlined here establishes that everything in the universe is nothing but a product of our conceptualization. Thus, when we take something to be otherwise—when we take it as not being a product of our concepts, but rather something that can exist through its own power—that's what we call “believing that something is real, or true.” If things actually existed in the way this state of mind thinks they do, then they would have to be things that existed through some nature of their own; or in truth; or in the other wording we've used above. It would seem that this text is rather difficult to comment upon correctly, for a number of reasons. record.english: As The Lantern states in clarifying the quotation from the Latter Part of the Secret Teaching where it says, "Noting is the secret three": The various sets of three--of sense power, object, and consciousness of the sense power--are what we call the "secret three"; that is, the three sets of five are an embodiment of the Five Families.  To note this fact is what they call "noting."

record.english: Invite then the Lama before you to come to the tip of your head; to do this, you can either use the secret words and sign called "bringing in the diamond," or you can simply visualize that They have come.  See Them melt then into your body from the top of your head, and imagine that the three of your own actions, words, and thoughts have been indivisibly melded into the enlightened body, speech, and mind of your Lama.  Use, finally, the hundred-syllable mantra to make all this very strong and firm. All of this you should repeat between successive sessions, and also at the start of a session. [Translator's note: The "secret words for bringing in the diamond" are given by Master Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra in his "Jewel of the True Thought of the Glorious Lady of Attainments," a Book of Instruction on the Brief Ritual of Fasting (ACIP digital text S06313) as: Om vajra samajah.  He describes the corresponding sacred gesture as follows: Cross your wrists.  Crook your two first fingers to look like hooks, and at the same time snap your fingers, using your thumb and your middle finger.]

record.english: The fourth topic has three parts: (1) A description of how we partake of the nectar that is produced when we engage in union with our Lady of Knowledge, and how this acts as a nutritive essence which strengthens the body; (2) How we use our tongue--as the diamond of enlightened speech--to stimulate the lower end of the partner's inner channel, and produce bliss in Her; and then use our tongue again to partake of the nectar that comes from Her because of this bliss; (3) How partners such as the Lady of the Lotus are pleased, and how we must be careful never to upset their minds--along with a concluding section. * * * Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) gives some additional, useful detail on the need for both inner and outer aids in his Book to Please Those with a Core of Goodness: A Brief Explanation of the Very Essence of "The Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps," on the Stage of Completion in the Teachings of the Glorious Secret Collection (ACIP digital text S00260, ff. 26b-27a):

record.english: And the expression "thousand petals," being a poeticism for the lotus, again recalls the line in scripture which reads, "...like the sprout of a lotus flower at the edge of the sea of wishes."  That is, the collection of goodness that we have done is similar to the spreading sprouts or blooms of a lotus upon the surface of the sea.  And what this goodness functions to do is that it steals the heart of every being--both my own heart and everyone else's--in the sense that it makes us happy.
